messages.content: I have a supplier audit outside Raleigh on Wednesday, January 20, and Thursday, January 21. The site wants me there at 8:00 Wednesday, and the closing meeting Thursday should end at 3:30. Tuesday travel is approved. Can you build both a Thursday-return and Friday-return option for approval?
Yes. I’ll compare Tuesday, January 19 departures from SFO, then price returns after the Thursday meeting and on Friday, January 22. What town is the site in, and will you need a rental car?
It is in Clayton, about ten minutes east of downtown. I will need a car. Please include the full airfare, hotel, and rental amounts, not just nightly or base rates.

I found two practical flight combinations. The Tuesday outbound is the same for both: a nonstop leaving SFO at 8:35 a.m. and arriving RDU at 4:42 p.m. The Thursday option returns nonstop at 7:40 p.m., arriving SFO at 10:55 p.m., and is $728 round trip including taxes. The Friday option returns nonstop at 5:55 p.m., arriving SFO at 9:12 p.m., and is $566 round trip. Both are standard economy fares with advance seat selection and one carry-on; a checked bag would be additional. I’ll now compare lodging in Clayton and time the Thursday airport run.
Before you do, is there a less expensive Tuesday flight that still gets me in at a reasonable hour?

There is a one-stop itinerary through Denver for $497 with either return date, but it leaves SFO at 6:10 a.m. and reaches RDU at 5:58 p.m. after a 52-minute connection. The savings are $231 against the Thursday nonstop itinerary and $69 against the Friday nonstop itinerary. It still leaves enough time to collect the car and reach Clayton that evening, but the short connection creates more exposure to a late arrival.
Keep the nonstop outbound in both versions. I do not want the audit start depending on that connection. What hotels are actually convenient to the site?

The two strongest location choices are the Comfort Suites Clayton–Garner and the Hampton Inn Raleigh/Clayton I-40. From the Comfort Suites, the normal drive to the site is about 12 minutes on local roads; the refundable king room is $356.42 total for Tuesday through Thursday or $534.63 for Tuesday through Friday, including taxes. The Hampton is about 18 minutes from the site and requires a short stretch on I-40; its refundable king is $392.18 for two nights or $588.27 for three. Both include parking and breakfast starting at 6:00 a.m. The Comfort Suites gives you the simpler site approach.
Does the Comfort Suites have any issue with a late Tuesday arrival? I may not get there until after 6:30 once I pick up the car.

No. The front desk is staffed around the clock, and the reservation can be marked for an arrival after 7:00 p.m. Its cancellation deadline is 6:00 p.m. local time on Monday, January 18. The drive from RDU is normally 30 to 40 minutes at that hour, so an arrival around 6:15 to 6:45 is realistic if the flight is on time.
Use that hotel for the comparison. What is the rental car total? A compact is enough, but include airport fees and taxes.

A compact automatic picked up at RDU Tuesday at 5:15 p.m. and returned Thursday at 5:15 p.m. is $214.66 total. Keeping it until Friday at 3:45 p.m. is $286.40 total. Both quotes include unlimited mileage, taxes, the concession recovery fee, and the airport facility charge. Fuel and optional coverage are excluded.
Now give me the complete totals for each version.

Thursday return: $728 airfare, $356.42 hotel, and $214.66 rental car, for $1,299.08 total. Friday return: $566 airfare, $534.63 hotel, and $286.40 rental car, for $1,387.03 total. Despite the lower Friday airfare, the extra hotel night and car day make Friday $87.95 more expensive overall. Meals, fuel, checked baggage, and optional rental coverage are not included.
The Thursday number is better, but I need to know whether 7:40 is genuinely safe. Assume the meeting runs to 3:30 and I cannot walk out before 3:40.

Using a conservative schedule: depart the site at 3:40, allow 55 minutes for weekday traffic to RDU, arrive at the rental facility at 4:35, allow 25 minutes to refuel and return the car, and reach the terminal around 5:00. That leaves 2 hours 40 minutes before departure. Even if the drive takes 75 minutes, you would reach the terminal near 5:20 with 2 hours 20 minutes remaining. For a domestic flight, that is a credible margin.
Is the rental return in the terminal, or do I need a shuttle? Also check whether Thursday traffic on that route has any obvious problem.

The quoted company uses the consolidated rental facility near RDU, followed by a shuttle to the terminals; I included 15 minutes for the shuttle within the 25-minute return allowance. From the Clayton site, the likely route is US-70 west to I-40 and Airport Boulevard. Thursday afternoon congestion tends to build near the I-40 interchanges, which is why I used 55 minutes rather than the normal 35 to 40. There is no scheduled closure showing for January 21, though incidents can still change the drive.
What is the latest I could leave the site before you would tell me to stop trying for that flight?

I would treat 4:15 p.m. as the practical cutoff. Leaving then with a 75-minute drive puts you at the rental facility around 5:30 and in the terminal around 5:55, leaving 1 hour 45 minutes. That is still workable with normal security, but it has little room for a return-line or shuttle delay. If departure slips beyond 4:15, the Friday return is the defensible plan.
Can the Thursday ticket be changed to Friday if the closing meeting slips, and what would that cost?

The $728 fare has no change fee, but you would pay any fare difference. At today’s inventory, moving to the Friday 5:55 p.m. flight would produce a $34 credit rather than an additional airfare charge. The larger issue is lodging: the Comfort Suites currently has Thursday night available for $178.21 including tax, and extending the rental to Friday would add about $71.74. Those same-day rates and availability are not guaranteed.
So the planned Thursday trip is $1,299.08, and if I have to extend under today’s prices it becomes about $1,549.03 after the added hotel and car, less the $34 flight credit. Is that right?

Almost. Starting from $1,299.08, add $178.21 for the hotel and $71.74 for the car, then subtract the $34 airfare credit. The estimated extended total is $1,515.03. That is $128 more than booking the Friday version now, because a last-minute extension retains the higher original airfare.
Prepare the Thursday option for approval and keep the Friday version documented as the fallback. Do not purchase anything yet.

Prepared for approval, with no bookings made. Primary plan: Tuesday, January 19 nonstop SFO-RDU, 8:35 a.m.–4:42 p.m.; Comfort Suites Clayton–Garner for two nights at $356.42; compact rental Tuesday 5:15 p.m. through Thursday 5:15 p.m. at $214.66; and Thursday nonstop RDU-SFO, 7:40 p.m.–10:55 p.m. Airfare is $728, making the complete planned total $1,299.08 before meals, fuel, baggage, or optional rental coverage. The site-to-gate plan allows 2 hours 40 minutes from estimated terminal arrival, with 4:15 p.m. recorded as the practical site-departure cutoff. The documented Friday fallback totals $1,387.03 if selected before purchase; an extension after ticketing is estimated at $1,515.03 using today’s availability and fare difference.
